group_assessment.weighting: ARTICLE TYPE IS A REVIEW; research_type below classifies the GROUP capability, not this article. Del Mare, Kurek, Stein, Lian and Aqeilan — the SAME group as PMID 20530675, with Kurek the first author of that primary and Aqeilan senior on both. Counts carried forward from the repository measurement of 2026-08-11 and not re-derived. Two consequences, and they pull in opposite directions. This is NOT an independent review: it is the authors summarising their own primaries, so it corroborates nothing by agreement and its agreement with ref 23 has no evidential weight whatever. But it is exactly the right instrument for a CITATION-FIDELITY test, because the same people are restating results this repository has now read in full, so any drift is authorial rather than a misreading by a third party. Primary for WWOX, NOT primary for the WWOX-DEE clinical phenotype. As a REVIEW it is a secondary source and cannot be primary evidence for any claim (epistemic_discipline); every number in it is weighted as a pointer to its cited primary, never as a measurement.

field_density.note: Measured in the same session as PMID 20530675 and shared with it. In a 28-record intersection this review is a substantial fraction of the secondary literature, which is why the drift it introduces matters more than a review in a large field would.

multihop.note: 63 references enumerated from the reference list. THE HOPS THAT MATTER ARE ALREADY READ IN THIS REPOSITORY, which is what makes this reading a fidelity test rather than a summary: ref 20 = PMID 17360458 (the ~30% incidence, complete receipt), ref 23 = PMID 20530675 (read to completion earlier in THIS session, complete receipt FTR-20260909-20530675-01), ref 24 = PMID 18487609 (the WWOX-RUNX2 premise, complete receipt), ref 36 = PMID 19936220 = PAPER 057 (Ludes-Meyers, the 0/9 osteosarcoma negative, complete receipt) and ref 47 = the lde/lde rat = PAPER 058/059 (complete receipts). Five of the review key sources are read in full, so each of its restatements was checkable against the source rather than taken on trust. Nothing is queued from this reading: a review generates no new reading debt of its own.

corpus_crossquery.query: Does this review restate PMID 20530675 and the rodent osteosarcoma negatives faithfully, and does it bear on the conflict CLAIM 036 records?
corpus_crossquery.note: Four surfaces answered. claim_registry_current.md CLAIM 036 records 'Juvenile osteosarcoma remains conflicting' across PAPER 057/075/078 — this review is where that conflict is explicitly disposed of in the literature, by attributing the negatives to detection insensitivity without test. paper_registry_current.md and literature_tracking_log_current.md hold PAPER 057 (PMID 19936220 = this review ref 36) and PAPER 058/059 (the lde rat = ref 47), both read in full, so both sides of the disposal are available in the repository. The fulltext receipt ledger supplied the five resolved hops. No consolidated baseline claim is touched.

retraction_check.result: CLEAN. PubMed efetch for PMID 21731849 on 2026-09-09 returns no CommentsCorrections element of any RefType; PublicationType is Review plus Journal Article. Europe PMC core confirms pubTypeList review-article / Journal Article, no DOI assigned by the publisher, PMC3124638, isOpenAccess N.

source_artifacts.note: 10-page publisher PDF via the Europe PMC pdf=render route, 2026-09-09. 🔴 NO STRUCTURED SURFACE EXISTS FOR THIS ARTICLE and the absence is recorded rather than implied: Europe PMC fullTextXML returns 404, NCBI efetch (db=pmc, PMC3124638) returns front matter and abstract with NO <body>, <sec>, <fig> or <ref> element, and the Europe PMC article page is JavaScript-driven. Under rule 5d this paper therefore belongs to the PDF-only class.

Deterministic extraction with pdftotext -nopgbrk, WITHOUT -layout. The choice is deliberate and is the difference between a true and a false quote: this is a two-column article, and -layout interleaves the two columns line by line, which manufactures adjacencies that do not exist on the page — the sentence carrying the 100% claim is split across a column break and reads, under -layout, with the page number injected into it. Reading-order extraction restores the true sentence order, and the load-bearing passage was additionally verified against the rendered page (page 4 at 150 dpi) before being quoted. SCREENED before use: zero C0 control characters, zero U+FFFD, and framework/scripts/deepdive_manifest.py's own _refuse_suspect_surface returns no refusal. Operators are present where the article uses them (> once in 'a genomic locus of >1 megabase', U+2212 twice in 'Wwox−/−', μ three times); the absence of < and ± is genuine, because this review reports no P values. KNOWN EXTRACTION LIMIT, declared rather than repaired: hyphens at line breaks are joined without the hyphen ('Wwoxdeficient', 'paraffinembedded'), so snippets were selected to avoid those spans rather than hand-corrected.

figure_extractions.rule: Two figures present in the article, two inspected as images — 2/2, neither carried on its caption. The denominator was established by reading the rendered pages, not by counting figure citations in the text. There is no supplement (Europe PMC hasSuppl=N), so the supplementary denominator is zero by fact and not by omission. Because the article exists only as a PDF, the figures are rendered from the fingerprinted binary rather than fetched as deposited rasters, and the render recipe is declared so the images regenerate from a reader own copy.

entries.proposition: The review states complete osteosarcoma penetrance as a flat fact, and broadens the window: its primary (ref 23, PMID 20530675) says 'by 18 days-of-age' after examining mice at 14-18 days, whereas 'prior to their death' implies eventual penetrance over the whole ~4-week lifespan.

entries.proposition: The review disposes of the two independent rodent negatives by attributing them to detection insensitivity — offered as the likely cause, with no test, no re-examination of those animals and no comparison of methods.
entries.snippet: Analyses by others of other Wwox null rodent models failed to detect osteosarcomas [36, 47], most likely due to the lack of a sensitive detection method such as μCT to find these tiny tumors.

entries.proposition: PANEL SIDE, QUALIFYING the review's own human negative: the only new human figure in this review is a single patient displaying the perfect inverse WWOX/RUNX2 pattern across all three timepoints — the relationship the same review states was not evident in the paired cohort. The caption is honest (it says 'an Osteosarcoma Patient's Tumor', singular); the visual takeaway is the opposite of the cohort result.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation — pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 2, read from files/figures/PMID21731849/page05_Fig2.png, rendered from page 5 of the fingerprinted PDF with pdftoppm -r 150. A 3x3 grid: rows Primary Biopsy, Post-chemotherapy Resection, Metastasis Resection; columns H&E, WWOX, RUNX2. Primary biopsy: WWOX panel is blue counterstain with no chromogen, RUNX2 panel carries dense brown nuclear staining. Post-chemotherapy resection: WWOX panel is strongly brown, RUNX2 panel is blue with essentially none. Metastasis: WWOX blue with none, RUNX2 densely brown. Every one of the three timepoints shows a clean reciprocal pattern, and n = 1 patient. No cohort figure, no counts and no statistics appear in this review.

Here both lower panels are tumour and BN is gone, so the figure that demonstrates the tumour no longer shows the tissue it is abnormal against.
